intendedObjective: Reconstruct the recording memo into clear editor instructions.
acceptableEditScope: Remove inflated language and organize policy, exceptions, unresolved matters, and initial checks without expanding them.
stableFactsAndClaims: Over the past month unclear filenames slowed excerpt selection; two door-labeled files contained footsteps followed by a closing door, without becoming unusable.
The naming policy applies to recordings made from 1 August onward and does not require renaming all existing files.
Old files may be renamed when used in projects if their original names are recorded in notes; delivered client files keep delivered names.
New names begin with the coordinator-assigned session code, followed by audible-action description and take number; editors must not invent replacement codes.
Descriptions identify audible action, not imagined use.
Location, equipment, and unusual conditions belong in text notes; uncertain sources must not be asserted as known, though notes may identify possibilities.
Joint-team session naming is unresolved; ask for a code before uploading and the coordinator keeps a list for later review.
The coordinator checks each team's first five new uploads for filenames and notes only; this neither assesses recording quality nor replaces the pre-client-delivery check.
protectedNamesNumbersDatesQuotesPhrases: first five new uploads from each team
ambiguity: Naming sessions jointly recorded by two teams remains unsettled.
voiceConstraints: Direct, practical policy language; distinguish mandatory rules, permissions, and unresolved questions.
